summary: Elevate your career in public service with our international relations and diplomacy training course. Gain essential skills for effective global engagement.
lede: International relations and diplomacy training prepares public officials to engage with foreign counterparts and intergovernmental bodies. It develops practical skills in diplomatic protocol, bilateral and multilateral negotiation, treaty and agreement drafting, intergovernmental procedures, and cross-cultural communication, with exercises in negotiation, official conduct, and diplomatic reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is built for public officials and government professionals who engage — or are preparing to engage — with foreign governments, regional bodies, and intergovernmental organizations. It is equally relevant to those who support diplomatic missions from within line ministries and those who represent their government directly at the negotiating table.
audience: Public Officials from line ministries (finance, health
modules: Treaty Drafting, MoUs, and International Agreements
Diplomatic Reporting, Briefing, and Capstone Mission
prerequisites: No formal qualifications in international relations or law are required. Participants should be practicing public officials or government employees with at least two years of professional experience in a government ministry, agency, or public institution. Basic familiarity with your government's foreign policy priorities is helpful but not mandatory. No legal training or prior diplomatic posting is required. Participants should bring a willingness to engage in role-play simulations, negotiation exercises, and group drafting workshops — active participation is central to the learning design.
